research_question: Does a measurable population of U.S. NAICS 54 employer firms with 10–99 employees exist?
decision_affected: Whether the project has a reproducible provisional research cohort.
supporting_result: An official table reports a nontrivial firm population for the exact industry, geography, year, and enterprise-size bands.
disconfirming_result: The population is absent, too small to recruit, or cannot be reproduced from an authoritative source.
preferred_source_type: U.S. Census administrative statistics with definitions and size bands.
evidence_standard: Original table opened; unit, geography, industry, year, bands, aggregation, and limitations recorded.
planned_queries: site:census.gov SUSB 2022 NAICS 54 enterprise employment size; search for revisions or errata
search_scope_and_stopping_rule: Stop after the current SUSB table, method page, release note, and revision notice are checked and the aggregation is reproducible.

research_question: Are firms with 20–99 employees more ready than firms with 10–19 employees for this sprint?
decision_affected: Whether to prioritize 20–99 in research recruitment and later messaging.
supporting_result: Direct observations show more qualifying handoffs, usable evidence, sponsor capacity, and buying behavior in 20–99 firms.
disconfirming_result: 10–19 firms qualify at the same or a higher rate, or size does not predict readiness after operational qualifiers are applied.
preferred_source_type: Authorized interviews and de-identified workflow observations; official size data are context only.
evidence_standard: Comparable observations across both size groups, using the same screener and explicit disconfirming cases.
planned_queries: lead response ownership by firm size professional services; small firm internal CRM workflow; AI adoption by firm size null or alternative explanations
search_scope_and_stopping_rule: Use official adoption data only to frame the hypothesis; stop the desk search after two independent current sources and resolve readiness through primary research.

research_question: Which role recognizes the problem, controls workflow changes, and can authorize a diagnostic sprint?
decision_affected: Primary buyer, website voice, CTA recipient, and buying-group map.
supporting_result: At least two independent participants in one role describe authority, a recent trigger, and a plausible evaluation or purchase process.
disconfirming_result: Authority is distributed, another role owns the decision, or no named role can authorize action.
preferred_source_type: Authorized role-diverse interviews plus organizational records or role descriptions.
evidence_standard: Evidence must distinguish problem experiencer, process owner, influencer, economic buyer, and approver.
planned_queries: inbound lead assignment owner B2B professional services; sales operations versus owner lead routing; who owns CRM process in small firms
search_scope_and_stopping_rule: Review relevant B2B scholarship and contrary ownership models, then stop desk research because role prevalence requires primary evidence.

research_question: Do qualifying firms show recurring breakdowns in capture, qualification, assignment, follow-up, handoff, or measurement?
decision_affected: Whether the proposed problem is real enough to map in the prototype.
supporting_result: Multiple independent firms show a recent, recurring, observable workflow gap in de-identified evidence.
disconfirming_result: Participants only agree in the abstract, events are isolated, or authorized records show a consistent process.
preferred_source_type: Authorized interviews and de-identified workflow evidence, supplemented by relevant peer-reviewed B2B research.
evidence_standard: Recent incidents, timestamps, fields, statuses, and handoffs; no customer content; prevalence claims require representative evidence.
planned_queries: B2B lead follow-up null result; CRM solves lead routing without consulting; marketing sales handoff no performance effect
search_scope_and_stopping_rule: Stop desk research after the key mechanism studies and at least one contrary or narrower interpretation; leave prevalence open for primary research.

research_question: Which observable conditions make a firm suitable for a bounded diagnostic?
decision_affected: Qualification rules and who the service is not for.
supporting_result: Recurring inbound inquiries, multiple participants, a usable system of record, de-identified evidence access, and a named owner predict feasible completion and action.
disconfirming_result: One or more qualifiers add no information, wrongly exclude feasible cases, or fail to predict usable evidence and implementation ownership.
preferred_source_type: Primary workflow walkthroughs and negative-case comparisons.
evidence_standard: Apply the same screener, record exceptions, and require an observable relationship between each retained qualifier and feasibility.
planned_queries: lead-response diagnostic prerequisites; process redesign readiness owner data; small B2B workflow evidence access
search_scope_and_stopping_rule: Stop after every qualifier has at least two confirming and one deliberately sought disconfirming case, or mark it unresolved.

research_question: Can a fixed-scope diagnostic and redesign create usable current-state and future-state artifacts?
decision_affected: Offer scope, deliverables, and whether a sprint is a plausible format.
supporting_result: Target-role participants identify the user, decision, and next action for each deliverable and prefer the bounded format to an alternative.
disconfirming_result: Artifacts are merely advisory, implementation needs dominate, or buyers prefer training, software, internal work, or open-ended support.
preferred_source_type: Peer-reviewed process literature plus moderated artifact walkthroughs with target roles.
evidence_standard: Literature may support method components; commercial format and usefulness require direct user evidence.
planned_queries: business process redesign failed implementation; diagnostic consulting limitations; lead workflow artifact usability
search_scope_and_stopping_rule: Stop desk research after method support and implementation cautions are documented; decide commercial format only after walkthrough evidence.

research_question: Does response timing materially affect outcomes in this segment, and what timing standard is appropriate?
decision_affected: Whether the offer or website may mention a response-time benchmark.
supporting_result: Segment-specific timestamp and disposition evidence supports a defined timing relationship after relevant confounders and uncertainty are documented.
disconfirming_result: No meaningful relationship appears, definitions vary, or the association disappears after context is considered.
preferred_source_type: Authorized de-identified operational data or a prospective test; older observational research is internal context only.
evidence_standard: Exact population, outcome, timing definition, model, uncertainty, alternative explanations, and current period are required for a numeric public claim.
planned_queries: lead response time replication B2B; five minute lead response critique; response time qualification confounding
search_scope_and_stopping_rule: Stop after tracing the viral statistic to its original sources and one independent critique; do not prescribe a benchmark without target-specific data.

research_question: What observable event makes the problem important enough to address now?
supporting_result: Multiple participants describe a recent event followed by concrete evaluation, time allocation, budget, or process-change behavior.
disconfirming_result: No action followed, other priorities consistently displaced it, or the stated trigger is hypothetical.
preferred_source_type: Critical-incident interviews and authorized internal decision records.
evidence_standard: Behavior is required; agreement that the topic is important does not establish urgency.
planned_queries: professional services lead response priority alternative; CRM process change postponed; small firm sales operations competing priorities
search_scope_and_stopping_rule: Stop secondary research after plausible alternatives are mapped; leave urgency unresolved until repeated first-party behavior is observed.

research_question: Will a qualified buyer pay for diagnosis and redesign, and at what scope or price?
decision_affected: Commercial viability, price, and whether pricing belongs on the website.
supporting_result: An authorized paid pilot, accepted proposal, deposit, or transparent price test produces observable commitment.
disconfirming_result: Qualified participants decline at feasible prices, demand implementation at the same price, or only express nonbinding interest.
preferred_source_type: Behavioral offer experiments and a delivery-cost model.
evidence_standard: Opinions alone are insufficient; test one clear scope and price at a time and record refusals.
planned_queries: fixed scope sales operations consulting price; professional services diagnostic willingness to pay; alternatives to paid CRM audit
search_scope_and_stopping_rule: Stop desk research after alternative price structures are mapped; require human approval before any external price or paid test.

research_question: Is a request for a 20-minute fit review an appropriate first commitment?
supporting_result: Representative participants understand the next step, accept the effort, and can complete a synthetic request without false expectations.
disconfirming_result: They prefer a lower-commitment artifact, misunderstand the educational status, or expect service acceptance or immediate advice.
preferred_source_type: Moderated usability tests and later controlled conversion behavior.
evidence_standard: Measure comprehension, trust, task completion, and expectation accuracy; do not infer preference from general CTA guidance.
planned_queries: B2B fit-review friction; consultation CTA alternative checklist; dark pattern urgency appointment request
search_scope_and_stopping_rule: Stop desk research after alternatives and deception risks are identified; choose through prototype testing.

research_question: Where may AI assist without weakening factual accuracy, privacy, or human accountability?
decision_affected: AI scope, data boundaries, review controls, and whether AI belongs in the offer name.
supporting_result: A use-case data map shows low-risk inputs, a named human reviewer, verification, failure handling, and reversible operation.
disconfirming_result: The use requires sensitive data, unsupervised external action, unverifiable output, or controls disproportionate to educational value.
preferred_source_type: NIST guidance plus use-case-specific privacy, security, and human review.
evidence_standard: Controls must be mapped to the actual use; guidance is not certification or proof of safety.
planned_queries: site:nist.gov NIST AI 600-1 verification provenance human oversight; generative AI workflow risk counterexamples
search_scope_and_stopping_rule: Stop after the official profile and relevant project data map are reviewed; escalate any sensitive or production use to a human decision.
status: policy context supported; use cases open

research_question: Which statements may appear on the reference website?
supporting_result: Each objective express or implied statement maps to relevant evidence that supports the exact population, outcome, period, and net impression.
disconfirming_result: The evidence is absent, secondary, mismatched, commercially conflicted, outdated for the claim, or supports only a narrower proposition.
preferred_source_type: Original evidence plus FTC policy and a human claim review.
evidence_standard: Every factual claim must have a claim-ledger row, appropriate prior substantiation, and a human reviewer; disclaimers cannot cure a misleading headline.
planned_queries: site:ftc.gov advertising substantiation objective implied claims reasonable basis; B2B advertising performance claim enforcement
search_scope_and_stopping_rule: Stop after current official FTC guidance and the relied-on source are traced; omit any claim that remains mismatched or unresolved.
status: policy supported; publication pending human review
